result.text:
All 57 tests pass. Here's what I built.

## Design

**1. Repeated commands** — `process_commands` now remembers the last command; `process_command_or_repetition` treats a digit as "repeat the last command `int(digit) + 2` more times" (`"a0"` → 3 advances). Only `a`, `t`, `h`, `g` are repeatable (`is_repeatable_command`), so `"0"`, `"a00"`, `"(0)"` are invalid commands. Each repetition goes through `process_command`, so every repeated movement is checked by the sonar on its own.

**2. Sonar and ground types** — `Sonar` (`src/surveycrawler/sonar.py`) answers the ground type of a position from a map keyed by `Point`, defaulting to firm sand; `Sonar.all_firm_sand()` / `Sonar.with_ground_types({...})`, injected through the new `SurveyCrawler.at_facing_with_sonar` (`at_facing` still works and uses an all-firm-sand sonar, which is why the original 16 tests are untouched). `GroundType` has three subclasses and two messages, so no conditional on ground type exists anywhere:

| | `move_crawler_to` | `turn_crawler_with` |
|---|---|---|
| `FirmSand` | changes position | evaluates the turn |
| `Boulder` | signals error | signals error |
| `Silt` | slides `randrange(10)` extra cells in the direction of travel | evaluates the turn |

Movements consult the ground of the destination, turns the ground the crawler is standing on. `Silt.with_random(...)` makes sliding testable.

**3. Guarded runs** — a state pattern: `CrawlerRun` with `FreeRun` and `GuardedRun`. The run decides what `(`, `)`, the end of the sequence, sliding on silt and an error mean. `GuardedRun` registers an undo action on every position/facing change; on error it puts the crawler back in a free run (so undoing registers nothing) and evaluates the undo actions in reverse. `process` wraps the sequence in a `try`, asks the current run to handle any error, then re-raises — so only the open guarded run is undone; movements before the `(` and in already-finished guarded runs stay. Undo actions never go through the sonar, so undoing cannot fail.

## Tests

`tests/test_survey_crawler.py`: the original 16 unchanged plus 41 new ones covering repetitions, the sonar (boulder in front/behind/underneath, a boulder stopping a repetition mid-way, sliding forwards and backwards, the sliding limit, turning on silt) and guarded runs (undoing moves, turns and repetitions; silt, invalid commands, nested and unfinished runs; `"aha(aagt3)aa(ht)"` with several runs; and the cases that must *not* be undone, such as `"(aa)x"` and `"a(aa"`). `FixedRandom` is the test double for sliding; one test uses a real `random.Random` over 100 runs to check the crawler always lands inside the sliding limit.

One judgment call worth flagging: the statement doesn't say what happens when the sliding on silt ends on a boulder or on more silt, so the sonar is consulted only for the position the command targets — the slide itself is not re-checked. The README's new section documents this and the rest of the design.
